dedupe_keys.name: grand ethiopian renaissance dam simulating filling new normal and drought risks on the nile nature communications

description: This case study is a Nature Communications paper on the risks and opportunities of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which will place two of the world's largest dams, the High Aswan Dam and the GERD, in two different countries. There is no agreement on how the dams will operate, so the authors simulate the reservoir filling period, a new normal period after filling and a severe multi-year drought after filling, and assess the effects on Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia. They find that the High Aswan reservoir could fall to levels not seen in recent decades during filling, although the risk of water shortage in Egypt is relatively low, that the new normal will benefit Ethiopia and Sudan without significantly affecting Egyptian water users, and that multi-year droughts will require careful coordination to keep harmful impacts small. Coverage: the three-country Nile system, scenario simulation, not observed data. Access: free article; the article is CC BY 4.0; the model name and data availability were not read beyond the abstract. Caveats: results depend on assumed operating rules and inflow scenarios. It informs transboundary reservoir operation and drought coordination simulations, and relates to satellite reservoir level data such as the DAHITI record in the catalogue.
